title: Scripture and Tradition
definition: Scripture and Tradition means all human traditions must be tested by God’s Word and kept beneath Scripture’s authority.
summary: Scripture and Tradition means all human traditions must be tested by God’s Word and kept beneath Scripture’s authority.
christFocus: Jesus corrected traditions that nullified God’s Word and called people back to true obedience from the heart.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Tradition can be helpful when it preserves faithful teaching, worship patterns, and wisdom from previous generations. But tradition becomes dangerous when it is treated as equal to or higher than Scripture.

Jesus confronted religious leaders who used tradition to avoid obedience to God’s commands. Scripture judges tradition, not the other way around. Every practice, system, and inherited habit must be brought under the Word.

Christ frees believers from man-made burdens while calling them into true obedience. Scripture and tradition helps the Church receive what is faithful, reject what is unbiblical, and remain centered on Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Church-hurt people often know what it feels like when human rules are treated as if they came from God. This doctrine helps separate the voice of Christ from the pressure of human control.

It also corrects the opposite error of rejecting all inherited wisdom simply because it is old. The question is not whether something is traditional, but whether it is faithful to Scripture.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Test traditions, habits, and church practices by God’s Word. Keep what helps you follow Christ faithfully, release what Scripture does not require, and refuse to bind others with burdens God has not given.
